content.value_statement: Creating Claude Code agents requires clear triggers, safe tool scopes, and structured prompts. This skill provides templates, examples, and validation guidance for maintainable plugin agents.
actual_capabilities: Explains the markdown and YAML structure for Claude Code agent files.
Shows how to write triggering descriptions with concrete examples.
Provides system prompt patterns for responsibilities, workflow, quality standards, and output format.
Documents model, color, and tool configuration choices for agents.
Includes complete example agents for review, tests, documentation, and security analysis.
Provides a shell validator for checking agent file structure and required fields.
limitations: It does not automatically prove that an agent behaves correctly at runtime.
The validator checks structure and simple text rules, not semantic prompt quality.
Example agents must be adapted to each project and tool policy.
It does not replace security review for agents with broad tool access.

use_cases.title: Create a plugin agent
use_cases.description: Create a new agent file with correct frontmatter, triggering examples, tool scope, and a structured system prompt.

use_cases.title: Standardize agent design
use_cases.description: Give a team shared patterns for agent naming, model choice, tool access, and review expectations.

use_cases.title: Validate agent files
use_cases.description: Check agent markdown files for required fields, valid values, prompt length, and triggering examples.

prompt_templates.title: Create a basic agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Claude Code agent for [task]. Include a name, trigger description, model choice, color, tool list, and system prompt outline.

prompt_templates.title: Improve triggering examples
prompt_templates.scenario: Refining when an agent should run
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this agent description and improve its triggering examples. Make each example specific, realistic, and tied to the agent purpose.

prompt_templates.title: Restrict agent tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this agent role and recommend the minimum tools it needs. Explain which tools should be excluded and why.

prompt_templates.title: Design a production agent suite
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a set of Claude Code agents for [workflow]. Define each agent purpose, trigger boundaries, tool scope, and validation approach.

output_examples.input: Create an agent that reviews TypeScript changes for quality and security issues.
output_examples.output: A reviewer agent plan with a clear trigger description, read-only tools, review responsibilities, severity guidance, and a structured report format.

output_examples.input: My test agent triggers too often and writes tests in the wrong style.
output_examples.output: Revised triggering examples, narrower activation rules, and prompt guidance that tells the agent to follow existing test conventions first.

output_examples.input: Validate this agent file before I add it to a plugin.
output_examples.output: A validation checklist covering frontmatter fields, prompt length, allowed model values, allowed colors, and missing triggering examples.

best_practices: Use specific trigger examples that show when the agent should and should not run.
Grant only the tools required for the agent role and expected workflow.
Define responsibilities, process steps, quality standards, output format, and edge cases.
anti_patterns: Using generic agent names or descriptions that overlap with other agents.
Granting broad tool access when the task only needs read-only analysis.
Writing vague system prompts without process steps or output expectations.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you design Claude Code plugin agents with proper frontmatter, triggers, system prompts, and validation checks.

faq.question: Does it create agents automatically?
faq.answer: It provides templates and guidance. An AI assistant can use them to draft agent files for your project.

faq.question: Can I use it with Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. Codex can read the guidance and help draft or review Claude Code agent definitions.

faq.question: How should I choose agent tools?
faq.answer: Start with the smallest tool set that supports the task. Add broader access only when the workflow requires it.

faq.question: What does the validator check?
faq.answer: It checks required fields, valid model and color values, prompt length, and basic description patterns.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude Code plugins?
faq.answer: The file format targets Claude Code plugins, but the prompt design guidance is useful for other agent systems.
